conventions.convention: M>0, |a|<M, r±=M±√(M²−a²), and the exterior manifold is R×(r+,∞)×S². The global tensor includes the rotation axis; polar charts exclude it. The horizon is introduced through a separate ingoing extension.
The Boyer–Lindquist cross term is 2g_tφ dt dφ, with g_tφ=−2Mar sin²θ/Σ. Azimuthal coordinates are real local lifts of the circle coordinate on intervals shorter than 2π.
The metric signature is (−,+,+,+), and the exterior future direction is selected by N=−sharp_g(dt). Smooth tangent-bundle conventions assume Countable Choice.

A rank-two Killing tensor is smooth and symmetric, with ∇_(a K_bc)=0 using the cyclic sum divided by three. Reducibility means a finite constant linear combination of the metric and symmetric products of lowered Killing fields.
The multiplier current is j_X^a=−S^{ab}X_b and its observer density is −g(n,j_X)=S(n,X), for a future unit timelike observer n. Neither conservation nor positivity is part of the definition.
In the ingoing extension χ=T+Ω_HΦ, Ω_H=a/(r+²+a²), and the compatible timelike field is Nbar=∂v−(2Mr/Σ)∂r. On the horizon g(χ,Nbar)=−1; no affine parametrization of χ is asserted.
Curvature uses R(X,Y)Z=∇X∇YZ−∇Y∇XZ−∇[X,Y]Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b=R^a_bcd∂a and Ric_bd=R^a_bad.

Hamilton–Jacobi separation solves g^{ab}∂aS∂bS=−μ² on an axis-avoiding open coordinate rectangle. Nonnegative radial and angular radicands give C¹ primitives with independently chosen signs; smoothness is claimed only where both radicands are positive. The radial expression contains (L−aE)²+Q.

The Kerr coordinate t is ct_SI and has length units. M and a are lengths; m_phys=c²M/G_N, J_phys=c³Ma/G_N, and physical horizon angular frequency is cΩ_H. The declared geometric Hamilton–Jacobi dimensions are [μ]=[E]=length, [L]=length², [Q]=length⁴, and [S]=length².

load_bearing.statement: For M>0 and |a|<M, defines the specified global symmetric Kerr tensor on R×(r+,∞)×S², with Σ=r²+a²ζ² and Δ=r²−2Mr+a²; nondegeneracy, signature, and time orientation are established separately.

The specified Kerr tensor is smooth, symmetric, nondegenerate, and has signature (−,+,+,+) throughout the exterior, including the axes; the explicitly given smooth field N=−sharp_g(dt) is timelike and defines a time orientation.

T and Φ are Killing. In a smooth ingoing extension, H+={r=r+} is null with future null normal generator χ=T+Ω_HΦ, Ω_H=a/(r+²+a²), and the specified compatible Nbar satisfies g(χ,Nbar)=−1 there. In the exterior polar chart T is spacelike exactly when r+<r<M+√(M²−a²cos²θ); the ergoregion has zero radial width at the axis.

For real E,L,μ,Q on the stated axis-avoiding exterior coordinate rectangle, nonnegative R(r)=[E(r²+a²)−aL]²−Δ[μ²r²+(L−aE)²+Q] and Θ(θ)=Q−cos²θ[a²(μ²−E²)+L²/sin²θ] give C¹ solutions S=−Et+Lφ+Sr+Sθ with Sr′=±√R/Δ and Sθ′=±√Θ. The branches are smooth where both radicands are strictly positive; no turning-point smoothness or global continuation is asserted.
For the specified Kerr exterior metric g, with M>0, |a|<M, and r>r+, the Ricci tensor of its metric-selected connection vanishes: Ric(g)=0, including the rotation axis by smooth extension.

Let K_ab be a smooth rank-two Killing tensor on a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection. Along an affinely parametrized geodesic γ:I→M on a connected open interval, K_ab(γ)v^av^b is constant.

For a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor S and a smooth Killing field X on an open set, defines j_X^a=−S^{ab}X_b and, for a future unit timelike observer n, ρ_X=−g(n,j_X)=S(n,X), without conservation or sign assumptions.

seams_checked.note: The horizon proposition's F5 uses the null-hypersurface normal and generator conventions supplied through def-gr-fx-null-screen-geometry and lem-gr-fx-null-normal-plane-and-screen. Its explicit ingoing metric establishes the null normal directly. It does not assume that χ is affinely parametrized or require a global ordered pair of null normals.

Opened def-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-mode and lem-gr-fx-kerr-horizon-modal-flux. They retain the supplied ingoing extension, compatible time orientation, Ω_H, and future normal χ. Their use of g(χ,T)=g(χ,Φ)=0 follows from normality and tangency. They impose the narrower rotating range 0<|a|<M and distinguish local mode traces and conditional flux identities from global wave existence or scattering amplification.
